name: Nunchaku
about: Technique names come from the Freestyle Nunchaku Wiki and the sources in the roadmap. Prerequisites and tiers are coaching proposals, not rules of the art.
careNote: Learn this on foam. It passes close to the head, neck or face, or leaves the hand.

branches.name: Spin
branches.blurb: Hand, wrist, finger and limb rolls, the wheel

branches.name: Finger pivots
branches.blurb: The supported route into finger rolls

skills.name: Front and back grip
skills.desc: Thumb toward the top, or little finger toward the top.
steps: Front grip: hold one stick like a hammer, thumb toward the link. The link leaves the top of your fist.
Back grip: turn the stick over so the little finger is toward the link. The link leaves the bottom of your fist.
Hold near the link end for control, or near the tail for reach.
Squeeze only as hard as the move needs, and keep the wrist loose.
watch: A tight grip that locks the wrist and tires the forearm
Holding the middle of the stick, which gives neither control nor reach
skills.drill: Let the free stick hang still. Change between front and back grip 20 times per hand without looking.

skills.name: Open grip
skills.desc: Stick held against the palm by the thumb; used for rolls and aerials.
steps: From a front grip, pin the stick against your palm with the thumb.
Open the four fingers flat while the thumb keeps the stick in place.
Close the fingers again without the stick shifting.
watch: Fingers curling back out of habit, which blocks rolls and releases
Pinching near the stick tip, so it levers out of the hand
skills.drill: Swing a slow circle. Open the fingers for one turn, close for one turn, 20 times.

skills.name: Plane map
skills.desc: Near and far walls, face, back, table, core, cavity: the language for describing a path.
steps: Walls are the planes at your sides. The near wall is on the side of the holding hand, the far wall on the other.
Face is in front of you, back is behind, roof is above and floor is below.
Table is a flat plane at waist height. High table is at the shoulders, low table at the knees.
Core runs down your centre line, and the cavity is the gap between arm and body.
watch: Mixing up near and far after changing hands: they swap with the hand
skills.drill: Call a plane out loud, then swing one slow circle on it. Go through all of them on each hand.

skills.name: Point and pivot circle swings
skills.desc: Striker circles with the hand still (point), or with the wrist circling too (pivot).
steps: Point swing: keep the hand and handle still and let only the striker circle from the handle tip.
Pivot swing: let the wrist and handle circle too, in a small circle, with the striker following.
Keep the circle flat on one plane and the speed even.
watch: The circle wobbling off its plane
Driving from the shoulder: the wrist should do the work
skills.drill: Ten point circles, then ten pivot circles, on the near wall. Repeat on the face and table planes.

skills.name: Six directions
skills.desc: Upspin, downspin, outspin, inspin, nearspin, farspin. Practise the overhead helicopter spin here too.
steps: On the wall plane: upspin rises at the front, as if striking upward. Downspin falls at the front.
On the face plane: outspin heads toward the near wall, inspin toward your centre.
On the table plane: nearspin heads toward the near wall, farspin toward the far wall.
For the overhead helicopter, raise the hand and circle on a flat plane above your head.
watch: Learning only your comfortable direction on each plane
Looking up at the nunchaku during overhead spins: keep your eyes forward
skills.drill: Ten slow circles in each of the six directions, on each hand, naming the direction as you go.

skills.name: Fades and stops
skills.desc: Slow the swing, then down stop, side stop, and the hardest, up stop.
steps: Fade: take speed out of a swing by letting the hand travel with the striker and easing off the wrist.
Down stop: fade until the striker hangs at 6 o'clock.
Side stop: stop the stick pointing out sideways, at 3 or 9 o'clock.
Up stop: stop at 12 o'clock. It is the hardest, because the stick must arrive with no speed left.
watch: Grabbing or tensing to kill the swing: a fade is gradual
The striker bouncing back after the stop, which means it arrived too fast
skills.drill: From a downspin circle, fade to a down stop within two turns. Then side stops, then up stops, 10 each.

skills.name: Six basic figure-8s
skills.desc: Nearspin and farspin V8, upspin and downspin H8, inspin and outspin H8.
steps: A figure-8 is two circles joined by a crossing, so the striker changes plane each half.
H8 traces an 8 lying on its side, wall to wall. Learn it with upspin, downspin, inspin and outspin.
V8 traces an upright 8, floor to roof. Learn it with nearspin and farspin.
Steer with small wrist movements and keep the arm quiet.
watch: Big arm swings instead of wrist work
One side of the 8 smaller or faster than the other
skills.drill: Think "over, under". Do 20 continuous 8s of one type, then reverse its direction for 20.

skills.name: 12 basic F8s
skills.desc: All six figure-8s in both front grip and back grip.
steps: Take each of the six figure-8s you know in front grip.
Repeat each one in back grip. The path is the same but the wrist leads differently.
That gives the 12 basic figure-8s.
watch: Avoiding back grip because it feels weak at first
The back-grip path drifting closer to the body
skills.drill: Pick one figure-8. Do 10 in front grip, change grip at a down stop, then 10 in back grip.

skills.name: Stretched and twisted F8
skills.desc: A wider gap between the two planes (stretch), or an angled path (T8).
steps: Stretch: move the two circles further apart, so the crossing covers more distance.
Twist: tilt the whole 8 to an angle between horizontal and vertical. This is the T8.
Change one thing at a time and keep the rhythm of the basic 8.
watch: Losing the crossing point, so the 8 becomes one big circle
Stretching with the shoulders hunched
skills.drill: Do five basic 8s, five stretched, five basic, five twisted, without stopping.

skills.name: Stalls
skills.desc: Turn the nunchaku to pause mid-swing and change direction; adapted from poi.
steps: A stall turns the nunchaku so it pauses during a swing, with its momentum gone.
Fade the swing first, then guide the stick to rest at the turning point.
Leave the pause in the opposite direction.
watch: Forcing the pause with a tight grip
Stalling at full speed: fade first
skills.drill: Swing, fade, stall at 3 o'clock, then leave in the other direction. Alternate sides for 20.

skills.name: BTB, BTH and UTL F8
skills.desc: Crossing moves behind the back, behind the head, or under a leg.
steps: Behind-the-back F8: circle on the near and far walls, with the crossing behind your back.
Behind-the-head F8: the same two walls, crossing behind the head.
Under-the-leg F8: crossing under the lifted far leg.
Walk the path slowly with the stick held in both hands before swinging it.
watch: Leaning forward to make room, which brings the head into the path
Rushing the crossing, where you cannot see the stick
skills.drill: On foam, do one basic 8 then one behind-the-back crossing, alternating, for 20.

skills.name: Straightjacket, sunshine, sweeper
skills.desc: Harder crossing paths through the far cavity, over the head, or between the legs.
steps: Straightjacket: behind the back, through the far cavity, then an 8 in front between the far wall and the core.
Sunshine: the crossing travels over the head, between the face and back planes.
Sweeper: the crossing passes between the legs.
Learn each as a slow walk-through first.
watch: Attempting these before behind-the-back 8s are reliable
skills.drill: Choose one. Alternate it with a behind-the-back 8 until you can do five in a row.

skills.name: F2B and B2F hand roll
skills.desc: 180° over the fingers; the most common way to change grip mid-spin.
steps: Start in an open front grip and flip the nunchaku over the hand, so the link crosses the back of the fingers.
Release the stick you hold and catch the other one as it comes around. That is front-to-back (F2B).
Flip it back the other way to return: back-to-front (B2F).
It travels 180° over the fingers and never touches the wrist.
watch: Throwing the roll upward instead of letting it travel around the hand
Closing the fingers too early and blocking the link
skills.drill: F2B, pause, B2F, pause. 20 clean pairs per hand before you remove the pauses.

skills.name: F8 hand-roll chain
skills.desc: F2B and B2F linked into a continuous loop.
steps: Do a front-to-back hand roll on one side of the body.
Carry the swing across and do a back-to-front roll on the other side.
Join them so the rolls replace the two circles of a figure-8.
watch: Pausing between the two rolls
The second roll starting before the first is caught
skills.drill: Count "roll, cross, roll, cross" at a slow, even tempo for one minute.

skills.name: B2B wrist roll
skills.desc: 360° around the wrist, back grip to back grip.
steps: Start in a back grip with the hand open.
Send the striker around the wrist for a full 360° and release the handle as it wraps.
Catch back in a back grip as the stick comes around.
Grip near the link end for tight control.
watch: The roll riding up the forearm: keep it at the wrist
Catching the wrong stick
skills.drill: Single roll, catch, reset. 20 per hand, then try two in a row.

skills.name: F2F wrist roll
skills.desc: 360° around the wrist, front grip to front grip.
steps: Start in a front grip with the hand open.
Send the striker around the wrist for a full 360° and release as it wraps.
Catch back in a front grip.
watch: Using a 180° hand roll and calling it done: this one goes all the way around the wrist
The elbow flaring out
skills.drill: Alternate one B2B roll and one F2F roll with a swing between, 10 pairs per hand.

skills.name: Continuous B2B and F2F chains
skills.desc: Loop the same roll without a break.
steps: Catch each roll in the same grip it started in, and send it straight into the next roll.
Add a little wrist drive each turn to replace the speed the roll loses.
Learn the continuous back-to-back chain first, then front-to-front.
watch: Speed dying after two or three rolls
Rolls drifting off the wrist as the chain goes on
skills.drill: Count your longest chain. Aim for 5, then 10, then 20 on each hand.

skills.name: 540° wrist roll
skills.desc: A grip switch with extra rotation.
steps: Start as for a 360° wrist roll, with more speed behind the release.
Let it travel one and a half turns.
Catch in the opposite grip: front becomes back, or back becomes front.
watch: Catching early at 360° out of habit
Adding height instead of rotation
skills.drill: Alternate a 360° roll and a 540° roll so you feel the difference in release speed.

skills.name: 720° and 1080° rolls
skills.desc: Named by degrees; needs more momentum behind the release.
steps: Build on the 540° roll with still more momentum.
720° is two full turns and 1080° is three.
Higher rolls depend on release speed more than on anything the hand does afterwards.
watch: Chasing rotation count before the 540° is reliable
skills.drill: Ten attempts at 720° per session. Log how many you catch.

skills.name: Finger roll
skills.desc: Roll around one or more fingers, often from a midgrip over the join.
steps: Take a midgrip, with the link or stick passing between two fingers.
Let the nunchaku roll around one or more fingers.
Catch as it completes the turn. Any finger works; on the thumb it is a thumb spin.
watch: A stiff finger: keep it relaxed but straight
Sore knuckles from wood sticks: learn on foam
skills.drill: One finger roll, catch, reset. 20 per hand, starting with the index finger.

skills.name: Thumb spin
skills.desc: A finger roll performed on the thumb.
steps: Set up as for a finger roll, with the thumb as the axis.
Roll the nunchaku around the thumb and catch.
watch: The stick sliding off the end of the thumb
Tucking the thumb in, which stops the roll
skills.drill: Alternate one index-finger roll and one thumb spin, 10 pairs.

skills.name: Round The Back Finger Spin
skills.desc: A finger spin path taken around the back.
steps: The sources I could read name this move but do not describe it, so find a demonstration before training it.
The name suggests a finger spin whose path travels around the back.
Have reliable finger rolls and a behind-the-back figure-8 before trying it.
watch: Guessing the mechanics and building a habit you later have to undo
skills.drill: Watch a demonstration frame by frame, then walk the path with the stick held still.

skills.name: Intercept
skills.desc: After a trick in the main hand, the other arm or a finger is put in the path of the chain to intercept it, often into a finger spin.
steps: The sources I could read name this move but do not describe it, so find a demonstration before training it.
In the snippets I found, the opposite arm, or a single finger of it, is placed in the path of the chain after a trick in the main hand, to intercept it into a finger spin.
watch: Putting a finger into a fast link on wood or chain: use foam and cord
skills.drill: With a slow swing on foam, practise placing one finger against the link and letting it wrap.

skills.name: Wheel
skills.desc: Spun on the link with one finger from each hand; easier on cord than chain.
steps: Place one finger of each hand on opposite sides of the link.
Spin the nunchaku between the two fingers. Only the link is touched.
It can turn upward or downward, named by the direction it rotates toward you.
Use a cord link of 3 to 4 inches: it is smoother than chain, and a short link makes the wheel very hard.
watch: Fingers drifting apart, which drops the nunchaku
Trying it on chain first
skills.drill: Hold the wheel for 5 turns, then 10, then 20, in each direction.

skills.name: Horizontal and disconnected wheel
skills.desc: A flat plane, or lifting one finger into a brief finger roll.
steps: Horizontal wheel: turn the wheel onto a flat, horizontal plane.
Disconnected wheel: lift one finger away for a moment, so it becomes a finger roll, then put it back.
watch: Losing speed during the tilt to horizontal
skills.drill: Five upright turns, tilt to horizontal for five, and back. Then add one finger lift.

skills.name: 360 horizontal and orbital wheel
skills.desc: Turn the body 360°, or revolve the wheel around the body.
steps: 360 horizontal wheel: keep a horizontal wheel going while your body turns a full circle.
Orbital wheel: carry the wheel around your body while it spins.
watch: Watching your feet instead of the wheel during the turn
skills.drill: Quarter turn, then half, then full, keeping the wheel alive each time.

skills.name: Arm and leg rolls
skills.desc: The same roll mechanics moved along the limb.
steps: Use the same release and catch as a wrist roll, with the forearm, upper arm or leg as the axis.
A larger axis takes longer to wrap, so release with more speed.
Catch with the same hand, or the other one.
watch: Bending the limb mid-roll, which changes the wrap
Catching too early
skills.drill: Forearm rolls first: 20 per arm. Then upper arm, then thigh.

skills.name: Neck roll
skills.desc: Roll around the neck. Learn it on foam only.
steps: A roll with the neck as the axis.
Keep the chin level and the release slow.
Use foam only, and cord, not chain.
watch: Any speed at all on wood or chain
Tilting the head into the stick
skills.drill: Drape and unwrap by hand first. Add a slow release only when the path is certain.

skills.name: Isolations
skills.desc: Tail and hand both rotate around the stick head; harder and less clean than in poi.
steps: In an isolation, the stick turns around its own head: the tail and your hand both circle that point.
Move the hand in a small circle that exactly cancels the stick's travel, so the head appears fixed in space.
It is harder and less clean than with poi, because the nunchaku has more points of rotation.
watch: The fixed point drifting
Expecting poi-level cleanness
skills.drill: In a mirror, pick a spot on the wall behind the stick head and keep the head on it for 10 turns.

skills.name: Swap
skills.desc: The handle moves between hands.
steps: Hold one stick with the other hanging still.
Place the stick you hold into the other hand and let go.
A swap moves the handle; a pass catches the striker.
watch: Swapping while the striker is still swinging
skills.drill: Swing, down stop, swap, swing on the new hand. 20 times.

skills.name: Shoulder pass (arm switch)
skills.desc: Flip over the shoulder, catch under the arm with the other hand. Done wrong it can strike your head.
steps: Hold one stick and flip the other backward over the same-side shoulder.
Reach the empty hand under that arm and catch the stick behind you.
Release the first hand and swing forward on the new side.
Repeat on the other side and speed up gradually.
watch: The stick clipping the head: send it over the shoulder, not past the ear
Catching too high. Keep the catching hand low
skills.drill: 20 slow passes alternating shoulders on foam, with a pause at each catch.

skills.name: Waist pass
skills.desc: A catch at waist height. The wiki lists it without a description.
steps: The sources I could read name this move but do not describe it, so find a demonstration before training it.
By its name, the catch happens at waist height.
Passes on the same plane flow together, so link it with other low passes.
watch: Catching in front of the body where the hands collide
skills.drill: Swing around the waist slowly and find where the empty hand meets the striker comfortably.

skills.name: Slick and gritch pass
skills.desc: Catch in the same grip as the handle (slick), or a different one (gritch).
steps: Slick pass: catch the striker in the same grip you hold the handle in, front to front or back to back.
Gritch pass (grip switch): catch in the other grip, front to back or back to front.
Decide the catching grip before the pass starts.
watch: Catching in whatever grip happens, without choosing
skills.drill: Shoulder passes: 10 slick, then 10 gritch, calling the catch grip out loud.

skills.name: Mirror pass
skills.desc: From one pass stance to its mirror, such as left shoulder to right shoulder.
steps: A pass stance is the position with a stick in each hand.
A mirror pass takes you from one stance to its mirror image, such as left shoulder to right shoulder.
watch: Uneven stances: the mirror should look the same on both sides
skills.drill: Hold each stance for a second in a mirror. 20 mirror passes.

skills.name: Back pass
skills.desc: Hand change behind the back. Keep the empty hand near the shoulder and the swinging hand at the lower back.
steps: Swing the striker behind your back.
Keep the empty hand close to the shoulder to catch.
Keep the swinging hand in line with the lower back.
Release and bring the nunchaku forward on the other side.
watch: Grabbing too high
Tight shoulders. If flexibility limits you, practise sliding the catching hand down from the shoulder
skills.drill: Without swinging, place the stick behind your back and change hands 20 times. Then add a slow swing.

skills.name: Under-the-leg pass
skills.desc: Swing under one leg and catch on the other side; start with a wide stance.
steps: Take a wide stance or lift one leg.
Swing the nunchaku under the leg.
Catch with the other hand on the far side.
watch: A narrow stance that leaves no room
Looking down and losing balance
skills.drill: Do the motion with an empty hand first, then 20 slow passes on foam.

skills.name: Flip switch
skills.desc: Release one handle mid-spin and catch the other as it wraps around the hand.
steps: Practise the throw first: swing the arm up a few inches and flick the wrist, so the link wraps the back of the hand.
Release one handle mid-spin.
Catch the other handle as it comes around the hand.
I could read only a summary of this tutorial, so check the steps against it.
watch: Flicking too hard, so the stick flies off
skills.drill: The practice throw alone, 20 per hand, before adding the catch.

skills.name: Elbow pass
skills.desc: Listed by the wiki without a description.
steps: The sources I could read name this move but do not describe it, so find a demonstration before training it.
Have a reliable back pass first: the wiki lists both in the same family.
watch: Elbow strikes on wood. Use foam
skills.drill: Watch a demonstration, then walk the path slowly with the stick held in both hands.

skills.name: Neck pass
skills.desc: Listed by the wiki without a description. Train on foam only.
steps: The sources I could read name this move but do not describe it, so find a demonstration before training it.
It passes around the neck, so treat it as a foam-only move.
watch: Speed, chain or wood anywhere near the neck
skills.drill: Drape the nunchaku around the neck and change hands by hand, with no swing, until the path is automatic.

skills.name: Side bounce pass
skills.desc: A pass entered from a bounce at the side.
steps: The sources I could read name this move but do not describe it, so find a demonstration before training it.
By its name, a bounce at your side redirects the striker into the pass.
Have a reliable limb bounce and shoulder pass first.
watch: Bouncing at full speed: fade into the bounce
skills.drill: Side bounce, pause, pass. Remove the pause once both halves are clean.

skills.name: Opposite arm spin
skills.desc: The main hand sends the nunchaku around the opposite wrist. Add more spins as you improve.
steps: The sources I could read name this move but do not describe it, so find a demonstration before training it.
In the snippets I found, the main hand propels the nunchaku around the opposite wrist. It follows a side bounce pass: one spin, then more as you improve.
watch: Adding spins before one is clean
skills.drill: One spin and catch, 10 times, before trying two.

skills.name: Drop pass
skills.desc: Trap the striker in a reverse armpit trap, drop the handle into the hand at the back, then free the striker.
steps: Swing the striker over the shoulder and around to the back.
Catch it in a reverse armpit trap.
Place the other hand behind the back, as for an upward back pass.
Drop the handle from above the shoulder into that hand, then free the striker from the trap.
watch: Dropping before the lower hand is in place
A loose trap that lets the striker slip
skills.drill: Do it in four counted stages: trap, place, drop, free.

skills.name: Pinwheel
skills.desc: A back pass and an over-the-head pass in one circular motion; adapted from staff.
steps: Do a behind-the-back pass.
Follow it with an over-the-head pass.
Join the two in one circular motion. It is adapted from staff spinning.
watch: A flat spot between the two passes
The overhead pass dipping toward the head
skills.drill: Back pass, pause, overhead pass, pause. Shorten the pauses over 20 repetitions.

skills.name: One-handed pass
skills.desc: The wiki lists it as a roll type but does not describe it.
steps: The sources I could read name this move but do not describe it, so find a demonstration before training it.
The wiki files it under rolls: the nunchaku changes grip or position using one hand only.
watch: Assuming it is the same as a hand roll
skills.drill: Look for a demonstration before training it.

skills.name: Armpit trap
skills.desc: The most common trap; catch the loose stick under the arm.
steps: Swing the nunchaku up and back beside the body.
Close the upper arm against the ribs to catch the loose stick under the arm.
Open the arm to release and swing again.
watch: Clamping late, so the stick bounces out
Raising the shoulder
skills.drill: Swing, trap, hold for a second, release. 20 per side.

skills.name: Hand, wrist, arm, shoulder bounce
skills.desc: Rebound the striker off the limb to change direction. Fade the swing into it.
steps: Fade the swing as the striker approaches the hand, wrist, arm or shoulder.
Let it meet the body with little or no impact, and let the body absorb what speed is left.
Send it back the way it came.
watch: Hitting yourself at speed and calling it a bounce
A stiff arm that cannot absorb
skills.drill: Forearm bounces on foam, 20 per side, at a speed where they are silent.

skills.name: Wrist, elbow and waist trap
skills.desc: Hold the nunchaku with a body part other than the hand.
steps: A trap holds the nunchaku with a body part other than the hand.
Wrist trap: catch against the wrist. Elbow trap: close the elbow on the stick. Waist trap: pin it against the waist.
Fade before the trap so it arrives slowly.
watch: Trapping at speed
Looking down at the trap
skills.drill: One trap type per session: swing, trap, hold, release, 20 times.

skills.name: Reverse armpit trap
skills.desc: Striker goes over the shoulder and around to the back; used in the drop pass.
steps: Swing the striker over the shoulder and around to the back.
Catch it under the arm from behind.
It is the trap used in the drop pass.
watch: Swinging past the shoulder blade instead of into the armpit
skills.drill: Over the shoulder, trap, hold, release forward. 20 per side.

skills.name: Chest, waist and leg bounce
skills.desc: The same fade and redirect on larger body areas.
steps: Use the same fade and redirect as a limb bounce.
The chest, waist and legs are larger and softer targets, so they absorb more.
Send the striker back along its path.
watch: Low bounces drifting toward the groin or knee cap
skills.drill: Thigh bounces first, 20 per side, then waist, then chest.

skills.name: Knee and chin trap
skills.desc: Smaller, less forgiving targets. Chin on foam only.
steps: Knee trap: catch the stick behind the bent knee.
Chin trap: pin the stick between chin and chest.
Both targets are small, so arrive slowly.
watch: Any speed toward the chin on wood
skills.drill: Place the stick in the trap by hand, release into a swing, and work backwards from there.

skills.name: Straight swing into bounce
skills.desc: Straight swings are not continuous, and most can end in a bounce. Chain them.
steps: Swing in a straight lane: a broad curve that starts in one place and ends in another.
End the swing in a bounce.
Use the rebound as the start of the next straight swing.
watch: Losing rhythm between swing and bounce
skills.drill: Chain four straight swings with four different bounce points.

skills.name: Neck, knee and foot bounce
skills.desc: The hardest contact points on the wiki list.
steps: These are the hardest contact points on the wiki's list.
The fade must be nearly complete before contact.
Neck on foam only.
watch: Bouncing off the knee cap: use the muscle above or below it
Any neck contact on wood or chain
skills.drill: Foot bounces: fade to almost a stop, then tap. 20 per side.

skills.name: Opposite-arm hook
skills.desc: A hook around the opposite arm above the elbow, from behind the body.
steps: The sources I could read name this move but do not describe it, so find a demonstration before training it.
In the snippets I found, the striker hooks around the opposite arm above the elbow, coming from behind the body.
watch: Elbow impact
skills.drill: Find a demonstration first, then place the hook by hand before swinging into it.

skills.name: Contact-staff style flow
skills.desc: Continuous body-led movement. The wiki names this only as a style influence.
steps: Link contact moves so the body leads the movement and free swings become rare.
The wiki names this only as a style influence from contact staff, so there is no set technique list.
watch: Forcing contact where a swing flows better
skills.drill: Improvise 30 seconds using only bounces, traps and rolls.

skills.name: Wrap and release
skills.desc: Capture the link around the hand, then release back into a swing.
steps: Let the link wrap around the back of the hand so both stick heads cross in the palm. The wiki calls this grip a handwrap.
Hold it for a beat.
Unwrap by releasing one stick back into a swing.
watch: Wrapping too tightly to release
skills.drill: Swing, wrap, hold, release, 20 per hand.

skills.name: Supported placement
skills.desc: Rest a stick on the body with a hand still close enough to save it.
steps: Fade to a stop.
Rest one stick on the forearm, shoulder or thigh.
Keep a hand within reach to save it.
watch: Placing while the nunchaku still has speed
skills.drill: Place, count three seconds, pick up into a swing. Five body positions.

skills.name: Short contact path
skills.desc: Let the stick travel a short way along the body before it leaves.
steps: From a placement, tilt the body part so the stick travels a short distance along it.
Catch it at the end of the path or let it drop into a swing.
watch: The path being left to chance: decide where it ends
skills.drill: Forearm: let the stick travel from wrist toward elbow and back, 10 times.

skills.name: Connected contact phrase
skills.desc: Several contact moves in a row, with no free swing between them.
steps: Join a placement, a short path and a bounce or trap.
Allow no free swing between them.
watch: Speeding up to hide gaps
skills.drill: Write down a three-move contact sequence and repeat it 10 times without a drop.

skills.name: Low toss and catch
skills.desc: Throw one stick up, let it flip, catch it. Start low and slow, over a bed.
steps: Hold one stick in an open grip.
Toss the nunchaku a short way up and let it flip.
Catch one stick as it comes down.
Start low and slow, on foam, over a bed.
watch: Throwing high before the catch is reliable
Reaching up for the catch: let it come to the hand
skills.drill: 20 tosses at chest height. Raise the height only after 18 of 20 are caught.

skills.name: Spin/aerial hybrid (SAH)
skills.desc: A cross between a roll and an aerial; exact mechanics unconfirmed.
steps: The sources I could read name this move but do not describe it, so find a demonstration before training it.
The name describes a cross between a roll and an aerial, and the snippets mention front-to-back and back-to-back versions.
watch: Inventing the mechanics from the name
skills.drill: Find a demonstration, then compare it with your hand roll and low toss.

skills.name: One-rotation aerial
skills.desc: Released in the air and caught after at least one full rotation, on each hand.
steps: Release the nunchaku into the air.
Let it make at least one full rotation.
Catch it cleanly, then learn it on the other hand.
This is what the WNA rules count as a high-risk technique.
watch: Counting a half rotation
Training only the strong hand: a routine needs it on both
skills.drill: 10 attempts per hand per session. Log catches, and aim for 8 of 10.

skills.name: Grip-change catch
skills.desc: Launch an aerial and catch it in the grip you want.
steps: Throw a one-rotation aerial.
Choose the catching grip, front or back, before you release.
Catch in that grip.
watch: Accepting whichever grip arrives
skills.drill: Call "front" or "back" before each throw. 10 of each.

skills.name: Pop and catapult
skills.desc: Throw and catch types the wiki lists but does not describe.
steps: The sources I could read name this move but do not describe it, so find a demonstration before training it.
The wiki lists pop and catapult as both throw types and catch types.
watch: Training from the name alone
skills.drill: Watch the aerials video and note how each release differs from a plain throw.

skills.name: Hang catch
skills.desc: A catch type the wiki lists but does not describe.
steps: The sources I could read name this move but do not describe it, so find a demonstration before training it.
The wiki lists hang as a type of catch.
watch: Training from the name alone
skills.drill: Watch the aerials video for catches that end with the nunchaku hanging.

skills.name: Clock-call releases
skills.desc: Name the clock position of the release and of the catch.
steps: Picture the swing as a clock face: 12 is the top of a vertical circle, or the far point of a horizontal one.
The numbers follow the direction of spin.
Name the release position and the catch position for each aerial.
watch: Forgetting that the clock flips when the spin direction changes
skills.drill: Release at 3 and catch at 9, then change one number at a time.

skills.name: Matrix Aerial
skills.desc: Bend forward, throw around the back, rise and catch on the opposite side with the same hand.
steps: Bend the torso forward to look at the ground.
Cross the throwing hand to the opposite side and throw the nunchaku around your back.
Rise to standing.
Catch on the opposite side with the same hand.
watch: Rising before the throw has left the hand
Trying it on wood
skills.drill: Rehearse the bend, cross and rise with no nunchaku, then with a foam pair at low speed.

skills.name: Reverse rebound
skills.desc: Tap the nunchaku in the air so it stalls and reverses direction.
steps: Throw an aerial.
Tap the nunchaku while it is in the air.
It stalls, then reverses its spin direction.
Catch it.
watch: Hitting instead of tapping, which knocks it away
skills.drill: Low toss, one tap, catch. Count how often the spin reverses.

skills.name: Partial reverse rebound
skills.desc: Only one stick reverses; the other keeps its direction.
steps: Set up as for a reverse rebound.
Tap so that only one stick reverses, while the other keeps its direction.
watch: Expecting it before the full reverse rebound is consistent
skills.drill: Alternate full and partial attempts, and note where on the stick each tap landed.

skills.name: Siteswap aerials
skills.desc: Plan aerials with juggling notation.
steps: Siteswap is a juggling notation that writes throws as numbers.
One performer on the wiki uses it to describe nunchaku aerials.
Use it to plan sequences of throws, once clock-call releases are reliable.
watch: Using notation to plan throws you cannot yet catch
skills.drill: Write a two-throw pattern, perform it 10 times, then change one throw.

skills.name: Opposite-hand catch
skills.desc: Throw with one hand and catch with the other, turning an aerial into a hand switch.
steps: Throw a one-rotation aerial from one hand.
Move the other hand under the falling nunchaku.
Catch with that hand.
watch: Both hands going for the catch
Throwing across the body too hard
skills.drill: Low throws from right to left and back, 20 times.

skills.name: Supported finger pivot
skills.desc: Pivot the stick around a finger while the thumb or palm still guards it. Leads into R8.
steps: Hold the stick in an open grip.
Let it pivot around one finger while the thumb or palm stays close as a guard.
Remove the guard a little at a time. It leads into the finger roll.
watch: Taking the guard away too soon
skills.drill: Quarter pivot, then half, then a full turn, 10 each.

skills.name: Weight shifts
skills.desc: Move weight between the feet in time with the swing.
steps: Stand with the feet shoulder width apart.
Shift your weight toward the side the nunchaku is on as it swings.
Shift back as it crosses.
watch: Locked knees
Shifting late
skills.drill: Figure-8s for one minute with a visible weight shift on every crossing.

skills.name: Steps and pivots
skills.desc: Step and turn without breaking the circle.
steps: Step in time with the swing, one step per circle.
Pivot on the ball of the foot to change facing.
Keep the circle on its plane as you turn.
watch: The swing stalling while the feet move
skills.drill: Four steps forward, pivot, four steps back, on a continuous figure-8.

skills.name: Travel
skills.desc: Cross the floor while linking moves.
steps: Link steps so you cross the floor while swinging.
Change direction with a pivot or a turn.
The WNA rules score use of the whole competition area.
watch: Performing on one spot
skills.drill: Mark a 3 metre square and visit all four corners in one unbroken sequence.

skills.name: Level changes
skills.desc: Drop and rise during a move.
steps: Bend the knees to drop during a move.
Rise during the next.
Keep the swing plane level relative to your body.
watch: Bending at the waist instead of the knees
skills.drill: Down for four counts, up for four counts, on a continuous overhead spin.

skills.name: Choreography
skills.desc: Set movement to the music.
steps: Choose a piece of music.
Set steps, pivots, travel and level changes to its phrases.
Rehearse the movement with no nunchaku, then add it.
watch: Choreographing tricks first and movement last
skills.drill: Walk the floor pattern for 30 seconds of music with empty hands.

skills.name: Path control
skills.desc: Trace a chosen shape cleanly at slow speed, in a mirror or on video.
steps: Pick a shape: a circle, an 8 or a straight lane.
Trace it slowly in a mirror or on video.
Compare what you traced with what you intended.
watch: Judging by feel alone
skills.drill: Film 10 slow circles from the front. Check that every one sits on the same plane.

skills.name: Isolation-like accents
skills.desc: Brief moments where the stick appears fixed while the hand moves.
steps: Take one beat of an isolation.
Place it inside a normal swing as a brief accent.
Return to the swing.
watch: Holding the accent so long that the momentum dies
skills.drill: Three swings, one isolation beat, repeat for one minute.

skills.name: Body and prop contrast
skills.desc: One moves sharply while the other stays calm.
steps: Move the body sharply while the nunchaku turns slowly, or the reverse.
Hold the contrast for a few beats.
Swap which one is calm.
watch: Body and prop always moving at the same speed
skills.drill: Slow overhead spin with a fast step sequence, then a still body with a fast figure-8.

skills.name: Lane linking
skills.desc: Move between swing pockets without losing the circle.
steps: A pocket is the space the striker circles in around your hand. A lane is a path that links two pockets.
Swing in one pocket.
Follow a lane to a second pocket without breaking the circle.
watch: Stopping between pockets
skills.drill: Near wall, overhead, far wall, and back, with no pause.

skills.name: Rolling figure-8
skills.desc: Figure-8 paths performed with wrist and hand rolls.
steps: Trace a figure-8.
Replace the circle on each side with a hand roll or wrist roll.
Keep the 8 the same shape as the plain version.
watch: The rolls shrinking the 8
skills.drill: Two plain 8s, two rolling 8s, alternating for one minute.

skills.name: Horizontal-to-vertical bridge
skills.desc: A simple linking move between a flat path and an upright one.
steps: The sources I could read name this move but do not describe it, so find a demonstration before training it.
The snippet I found calls it a simple way to bridge a horizontal path and a vertical one.
watch: Forcing the plane change with the arm
skills.drill: From an overhead spin, find the gentlest way down into a wall-plane circle, and repeat it.

skills.name: Trick progression drill
skills.desc: Start with a side bounce pass into one opposite arm spin, then add one element at a time.
steps: Start with a side bounce pass into one opposite arm spin.
Add one element at a time, such as a second spin.
This structure comes from a snippet I could not read in full.
watch: Adding before the current version is clean
skills.drill: Repeat the current version five times clean before each addition.

skills.name: Turns
skills.desc: Rotate the body during a freestyle, which also covers more area.
steps: Use a pass or a crossing as the moment to rotate the body.
Turn with the swing, not against it.
I could read only a summary of this tutorial.
watch: Getting dizzy: spot a point on the wall
skills.drill: Quarter turns on every shoulder pass, then half turns.

skills.name: Tempo changes
skills.desc: Slow and fast sections that follow changes of pace in the music.
steps: Use fades to slow a section.
Use wrist drive to speed one up.
Match the changes to the music. The WNA rules score tempo and rhythm.
watch: One speed throughout
skills.drill: Eight counts slow, eight counts fast, on one repeated move.

skills.name: Flairs
skills.desc: Novelty moves that fit no other group.
steps: A flair is any novelty move that fits no other group.
Collect ideas from other props and from your own mistakes.
Place one where the routine needs surprise.
watch: Stacking flairs so nothing stands out
skills.drill: Invent one new flair a week and film it.

skills.name: Gap filling
skills.desc: Fit extra tricks, often digit tricks, into gaps between moves.
steps: Find a gap between two moves.
Fit a small trick, often a finger trick, into it.
This approach is described in snippets I could not read in full.
watch: Filling every gap, which leaves no breathing room
skills.drill: Take a loop you know and add one finger roll at its slowest point.

skills.name: Personal style
skills.desc: Pick a direction: fast and aggressive, or slow and fluid with poi, dance or contact influence.
steps: Watch performers with contrasting styles.
Decide between fast and aggressive, or slow and fluid.
Choose moves, tempo and link type to suit: chain for fast styles, cord for fluid ones.
watch: Copying one performer move for move
skills.drill: Film one minute of freestyle each month and note what looks like you.

skills.name: Competition routine
skills.desc: 90 to 180 seconds under WNA rules, to music, using the whole area.
steps: Build a piece of 90 to 180 seconds to music.
Include single and double sections: leaving either out costs 2.0 points.
Include a one-rotation aerial on each hand, and one with both nunchaku in the air.
Use the whole area, and avoid drops and freezes of 3 seconds or more.
watch: Building for a different event's rules: confirm yours first
skills.drill: Run the full piece and log drops. Aim for four clean runs in five.

skills.name: Two-skill bridge
skills.desc: Join two known moves, tested in both directions where possible.
steps: Choose two moves you can do.
Find where the first ends: hand, grip, plane and direction.
Start the second from exactly there.
watch: Resetting between the moves
skills.drill: A to B, 10 times, then B to A.

skills.name: Loop
skills.desc: A bridge that returns to its start, so it can repeat.
steps: Take a bridge.
Add a link from the end back to the start.
Repeat it without stopping.
watch: A hidden reset inside the loop
skills.drill: Run the loop for one minute.

skills.name: Signature phrase
skills.desc: A complete personal sequence with a clean entry and exit.
steps: Choose a loop or bridge that feels like yours.
Give it a clean entry and a clean exit.
Vary its tempo.
watch: A phrase that only works from one starting position
skills.drill: Enter the phrase from three different moves.

skills.name: Two-stick handling
skills.desc: Includes "adjust the chucks", and swinging one stick while the other stays controlled.
steps: Hold one nunchaku in each hand.
Swing one while the other stays trapped or hanging still.
Change over.
Practise re-gripping both to the same hold. The belt sheet calls this "adjust the chucks".
watch: Both sticks drifting toward the centre line
skills.drill: Ten circles on the right with the left still, then swap. Repeat with figure-8s.

skills.name: Double, side and diagonal strikes
skills.desc: Traditional basics from a green belt sheet; a good timing drill.
steps: Double strikes: both nunchaku strike together.
Alternating side strikes: one after the other.
Downward diagonal strikes, on each side.
These come from a green belt testing sheet.
watch: The sticks meeting in the middle
skills.drill: Ten of each, front view and side view in a mirror.

skills.name: Alternating outward figure-8
skills.desc: One stick after the other, at a fixed offset.
steps: Do an outward figure-8 with one hand.
Start the same figure-8 with the other hand half a beat later.
Keep the offset fixed.
watch: The offset closing until the sticks collide
skills.drill: Count "one and two and", right hand on the numbers and left on the "and".

skills.name: Synchronized mode
skills.desc: The same technique on both sides, at the same moment.
steps: Choose one move.
Do it with both hands at the same moment.
Keep the nunchaku on separate planes at each side.
watch: One hand leading the other
skills.drill: Synchronized wall-plane circles for one minute, then figure-8s.

skills.name: Unsynchronized mode
skills.desc: The same technique with one hand delayed.
steps: Choose one move.
Start one hand, then start the other half a cycle later.
Hold the delay steady.
watch: Drifting back into sync
skills.drill: Swap between synchronized and unsynchronized circles every eight counts.

skills.name: Three-beat downward weave
skills.desc: Sticks and wrists cross alternately, like two figure-8s.
steps: The two nunchaku and the two wrists cross over each other in turn, like two separate figure-8s.
Spinning downward, count three beats on each side.
It is adapted from poi, and the three-beat downward weave is the basic version.
watch: Hands too far apart to cross
The sticks colliding when the timing slips
skills.drill: Learn it with both sticks held in one hand as a single figure-8, then split the hands.

skills.name: Upward; four- and five-beat weaves
skills.desc: Reversed direction, or more beats on each side.
steps: Upward weave: the same crossing with the spin reversed.
Four-beat and five-beat weaves: more beats on each side.
watch: Losing count of the beats
skills.drill: Three-beat for eight cycles, then one cycle of four-beat.

skills.name: Butterfly
skills.desc: Poi-derived. In poi, the two move in opposite directions.
steps: It is adapted from poi, where the two props move in opposite directions.
The hands stay close together.
The wiki names the move without describing it.
watch: The sticks meeting at the top and bottom of the circles
skills.drill: Find a poi butterfly tutorial and work through it slowly with foam.

skills.name: Windmill
skills.desc: Poi-derived. In poi, the two follow each other the same way on an upright plane, passing above the head.
steps: It is adapted from poi, where a windmill is a reel in which the props pass above the head, following each other in the same direction on an upright plane.
The wiki names the move without describing it.
watch: Dipping the circles toward the head
skills.drill: Find a poi windmill tutorial and work through it with foam.

skills.name: Double wrist rolls
skills.desc: Keep hips fixed, then move them with intent, and work the full range.
steps: Learn the wrist roll on one nunchaku first.
Do it on both hands, with the hips kept still.
Then move the hips deliberately.
Work through the full range: wider and higher rolls lead into other moves.
watch: The weak hand falling behind
skills.drill: Synchronized back-to-back rolls, counting pairs caught.

skills.name: Double bounces and traps
skills.desc: Single-stick contact moves with a stick in each hand.
steps: Take a bounce or trap you know on one nunchaku.
Do it on both sides together.
Then do it alternately.
watch: Crossing arms into the other stick's path
skills.drill: Double armpit traps and releases, 20 times.

skills.name: Double Dragons kata
skills.desc: An optional traditional track: a set form with footwork.
steps: A set form for two nunchaku, with footwork.
It is tested on the green belt sheet, which does not list its moves.
Learn it from an instructor or the programme it belongs to.
watch: Learning the form from a description alone
skills.drill: Practise the sheet's doubles footwork exercise.

skills.name: Different move on each hand
skills.desc: The third doubles mode, and the hardest for timing.
steps: Give each hand a different move.
Start with a simple pairing: a circle on one side and a figure-8 on the other.
Timing keeps the sticks apart.
watch: Both hands drifting toward the same move
skills.drill: Hold the pairing for 20 counts, then swap hands.

skills.name: One-stick aerial, other spinning
skills.desc: The step that makes doubles passes possible.
steps: Keep one nunchaku circling.
Throw a one-rotation aerial with the other.
Catch it without the circle changing.
watch: The circling hand freezing during the throw
skills.drill: 10 throws per hand, with the other hand keeping a steady count.

skills.name: Air pass or swap
skills.desc: A pass or swap done while one nunchaku is in the air.
steps: Passes and swaps normally need a free hand, so with two nunchaku they only work while one is in the air.
Throw one nunchaku.
Pass or swap the other before the first comes down, then catch.
watch: Rushing the pass and missing the catch
skills.drill: Throw, clap, catch first. Then replace the clap with a swap.

skills.name: Both sticks in the air
skills.desc: Both airborne at once for at least one full rotation.
steps: Release both nunchaku.
Each must make at least one full rotation while both are in the air together.
Catch both.
The WNA rules require this in the two-nunchaku part of a routine.
watch: Throwing them into each other: keep each on its own side
skills.drill: Low synchronized throws. Aim for 5 of 10, then 8 of 10.

skills.name: Double isolations
skills.desc: Possible only to a limited extent.
steps: Do an isolation with each hand.
The wiki says this is possible only to a limited extent, and that poi gives a better effect.
watch: Spending much time here before the single isolation is clean
skills.drill: One hand isolating while the other circles normally.

phases.name: Swing control
phases.skills: F1 F2 F3 F4 F5 F6 F7 S1 C1 M1
phases.gate: All six figure-8s on the strong hand, plus a side stop on demand

phases.name: Core flow
phases.skills: R1 R2 R3 S2 S3 S4 C2 C3 L1 L11
phases.gate: One minute without a drop, linking a hand-roll chain, a shoulder pass and a limb bounce

phases.name: Branch entry
phases.skills: R4 R5 R8 S5 S6 S7 S8 C4 C5 C6 C7 A1 A2 A3
phases.gate: A back pass, continuous wrist rolls, and a one-rotation aerial on each hand

phases.name: Doubles entry
phases.skills: D1 D2 D3 D4 D5 D6 A4 A5 A6 A7 R12 M3 M4
phases.gate: F7 and R5 on the weak hand, then a three-beat weave for one minute without collisions

phases.name: Routine
phases.gate: A 90-second piece to music, with single and double sections and all required risk moves

weeks.result: Two signature candidates with usable entries and exits

weeks.focus: Compare reliability, style and rule fit
weeks.result: Primary combo plus a simpler alternate
